title: Course 10 checkpoint — CI/CD, Infrastructure, and AI DevOps

questions.prompt: Why promote an image digest rather than rebuild from the same commit for production?
options: The existing evidence covers the exact bytes promoted
questions.explanation: A rebuild creates a different artifact subject and can use changed dependencies or infrastructure; promoting the verified digest preserves evidence identity.

questions.prompt: What does a valid provenance attestation establish by itself?
options: How an identified artifact was built under stated identity and inputs
questions.explanation: Provenance supports origin and build-process verification; consumers still need security, quality, compatibility, authorization, and risk policy.

questions.prompt: An evaluation service is unavailable during release admission. What disposition is most accurate?
options: Inconclusive because required evidence is missing
questions.explanation: Unavailable evidence does not prove regression or success; the gate is inconclusive and promotion waits for trustworthy evidence or an authorized bounded exception.

questions.prompt: Which OIDC trust condition best prevents a feature branch from using the production role?
options: A subject bound to the protected production environment or exact ref
questions.explanation: The cloud trust policy should bind subject and audience to the expected repository plus protected environment/ref, and ideally the governed reusable workflow.

questions.prompt: Why pin a third-party GitHub Action to a full commit SHA?
options: It makes that dependency reference immutable
questions.explanation: A version tag can move; a verified full commit SHA fixes the referenced action revision, although source and permissions still require review.

questions.prompt: Why must automation apply the exact reviewed Terraform plan?
options: A new plan can differ because state, inputs, providers, or configuration changed
questions.explanation: Re-planning at apply time breaks the link between approval and effect; changes to state or inputs require a newly inspected plan.

questions.prompt: A Terraform variable is marked sensitive. What remains true?
options: Its value can never enter state
It may still be stored in plan or state and those artifacts need protection
questions.explanation: Sensitive marking primarily redacts presentation; use ephemeral/write-only mechanisms where suitable and protect plans and remote state as restricted data.

questions.prompt: A canary has zero errors after 20 requests but policy requires 200. What should happen?
options: Remain inconclusive until the predeclared evidence requirement is met
questions.explanation: A tiny sample creates false confidence; minimum population and horizon are part of the versioned rollout decision contract.

questions.prompt: A canary improves latency but produces one confirmed forbidden outcome. What should the hard safety gate do?
questions.explanation: A forbidden outcome is not compensated by performance gains; the predeclared safety invariant stops exposure and initiates response.

questions.prompt: Why is rolling back only the container tag insufficient for an AI release?
options: Model, prompt, policy, data/index, and infrastructure may remain incompatible
questions.explanation: Recovery must restore a verified compatible release graph, not one component whose surrounding contracts may have changed.

options: Maximum acceptable data loss measured in time
questions.explanation: RPO bounds the amount of state that may be lost; RTO separately bounds how long restoration may take.

questions.prompt: A restore meets RTO and RPO but tenant authorization was not retested. Is the drill complete?
options: No; integrity and authorization must also be verified
questions.explanation: Availability and data timing do not prove a safe restore; access control and tenant isolation must be revalidated before declaring recovery.
